# The Hugging Face surface, and what this hub does with it

Every operation Hugging Face documents in [its own machine-readable specification](https://huggingface.co/.well-known/openapi.json), with one verdict each. The specification is the authority for how wide the surface is. It is not the authority for the shape of a response, and it cannot be: the two routes clients ask for most, `GET /api/models` and `GET /api/models/{repo}`, are not in it. Recorded client transcripts are the authority for shape, and this map does not stand in for them.

| Read on | 2026-11-15 |

## The verdicts

| Verdict | Count | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `answered` | 6 | Answered from the hub's own index, without asking huggingface.co. |
| `partial` | 1 | Answered from the index, with the fields the record cannot supply named in an X-Hub-Partial header, so a client is never given an invented value. |
| `passthrough` | 25 | Relayed to huggingface.co and returned. A client cannot tell the difference, so drop-in holds; nothing was served from the index, so decentralization does not. |
| `refused` | 36 | Refused with a typed code from the kernel's closed set. Where that code is not the one Hugging Face sends for the same case, the row or a finding says so. |
| `unreachable` | 9 | Cannot be reached through HF_ENDPOINT at all, whatever the hub builds, because the client hardcodes huggingface.co. |
| `out-of-scope` | 302 | Deliberately not a hub concern. |

There is no verdict for "answered, but narrower than Hugging Face's answer and silent about it". That is a defect rather than a position, so where the hub does it the row carries a note and the note is collected under [Findings](#findings).

## What these verdicts are worth

Every verdict here about what the hub does was read from edge/edge.mjs on 2026-11-15, not measured against a running edge. The routing it describes is one branch: any path under /api/models/ that is not a write route reaches fromIndex(), and what fromIndex() cannot answer is relayed to huggingface.co, because useHuggingFace defaults to true. A POST under that branch other than paths-info is refused 400 BadRequest. Anything the branch does not match is refused 400 BadRequest. Where an operation's path carries {repoType}, the verdict is what a client sees when repoType is models, the only kind this hub holds.

## Findings

- **`GET /api/models/{namespace}/{repo}/refs`** — The hub answers refs with branches naming main and empty tags, converts and pull requests, and unlike the commits route it sends no X-Hub-Partial header, so a client cannot tell the list is narrower than Hugging Face's rather than genuinely empty. Read from edge/edge.mjs; a candidate for the honesty rule HK-15 states.
- **`GET /api/whoami-v2`** — site_spec.py lists whoami-v2 as part of the read surface, described as who the token belongs to, and the hub always refuses it. The description promises more than the hub does, even though the refusal itself is correct.
- **`HEAD /{repo}/resolve/{revision}/{path}`** — HEAD on the resolve route is the single most important operation for huggingface_hub, which raises FileMetadataError without those three headers on the first response, and Hugging Face's own specification does not document it. Only a recorded transcript settles its shape.
- **`GET /api/models`** — The listing every client and every page depends on is absent from Hugging Face's published specification, so its query names, row shape and Link-header cursor are known here only from reading clients and from HK-15 and HK-16.
- **`GET /api/models/{repo}`** — Model information is absent from the published specification. The hub's answer is shaped from recorded client reads, and HK-15 is what keeps it from inventing a field.
- **`GET /api/models/{repo}/revision/{revision}`** — Absent from the published specification for models, though the same route is documented for the kernels repository kind.
- Every write the hub refuses is refused 400 BadRequest, because the fallthrough answer is the kernel's any-other case. Hugging Face answers an unauthenticated write with 401 or 403, so huggingface_hub raises a different exception against the hub than against Hugging Face for the same call. The refusal is typed and modelled, and it is the wrong type for drop-in. Read from edge/edge.mjs and app/tools/site_spec.py on 2026-11-15.
- Any method other than POST under /api/models/ that the index cannot answer is relayed to huggingface.co, DELETE, PUT and PATCH included, with no token attached. Nothing can be destroyed, because the hub holds no credential, but a client's DELETE receives Hugging Face's 401 rather than the hub's typed refusal, and the hub makes an outbound request it could have refused locally. Read from edge/edge.mjs on 2026-11-15.
- The relay is the default: useHuggingFace is true unless the edge is configured otherwise, so a passthrough verdict describes the shipped configuration. An edge run with the relay off refuses all 25 of those operations instead and answers the listing from the browse index. So the decentralization claim rests on a configuration in which 25 of the 32 operations this map calls answered in some form become refusals, and only 7 survive. Counted from this map; not measured against a running edge.

Revoking a Hugging Face credential, which the hub never holds. Default verdict `out-of-scope`.

| Verdict | Operation | What Hugging Face calls it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `out-of-scope` | `POST /api/credentials/revoke` | Revoke leaked tokens |
